items.title: What GGSocial is: brands, channels and the desk
items.body: GGSocial is one desk for every brand you run. It lets a team plan, approve, schedule and publish social content for many companies without a separate login for each. The core unit is the brand: one company or project, with its own channels, media, calendar, team and timezone. A channel is one account on one platform, owned by one brand. Some channels are live: GGSocial publishes to them itself through the platform's API. Others are manual-only, because the platform has no write API for organic content. For those, GGSocial still composes, validates, schedules and queues the post and gives a person copy-ready blocks to post themselves. A manual-only channel gets the same validation, calendar slot and approval flow as a live one and simply ends with a person clicking publish. People sign in with an email and a password.

items.title: Writing and planning: composer, calendar, playbook
items.body: The Composer lets you write base copy once and override it per channel, with live character counts and per-platform rules: Reddit needs a title and a subreddit, YouTube needs a title, Instagram needs media, and X caps at 280 characters and can thread on blank lines. The Calendar shows every brand on one month grid, colour-coded, and a post can be dragged to move it. A post's scheduled time is an absolute instant shown in the brand's timezone. The Playbook holds master instructions for each format and kind of engagement, with limits the app checks itself such as title words, hashtag count, copy length, aspect ratio and posting windows; scheduling and approval refuse a post that breaks a rule marked as a must. Analytics shows what went out, where, and whatever metrics the platform returns.

items.title: Approvals, roles and the publish queue
items.body: A post moves from draft to needs approval to approved to scheduled, with comments and change requests along the way. Roles are per brand: owner (everything, including archiving the brand), admin (channels, team and content), editor (write, schedule and publish), approver (review only, cannot edit) and viewer (read-only). Editing and publishing need editor or above; managing channels, team and the brand needs admin or above; approving is for the approver role or admin and above. Every server action re-checks the role, because hiding a button in the screen is not the security boundary. The Publish queue holds anything due on a manual-only channel, with copy buttons, the media to download and platform-specific steps. Ticking a queue item off marks it published.

items.title: Agents and the Review inbox
items.body: Each brand can switch on a crew of agents that do hourly work so people only set guidelines and review. There are four: the content strategist (keeps the content plan ahead of the calendar), the content writer (keeps the calendar full from the plan, books posts into open slots and revises work sent back), the community manager (drafts replies to comments, messages, mentions and reviews and flags anything a person must decide) and the performance analyst (reads yesterday's posts each morning and writes weekly and monthly reports). Review is on for every step until the brand owner switches it off, and the reason is kept in the log. A reviewer scores agent output out of 100 and flags risks; weak but safe work goes back to the agent once with fixes. Safety stops pause a run whatever the setting: a flagged risk such as prices, refunds, legal or health matters, a score under the pass mark, a broken playbook rule marked as a must, the reviewer being unable to run, the daily AI budget being spent, or a step that keeps failing. Everything waiting on a person lands in one Review inbox, where you can approve, send back with a note, or stop the run. Every Claude call is logged with its cost.
